outcome: Fix the PR #3 review finding on repeated join key casts: following the advice for a second join on the same text key must reuse the cast column the first rewrite made, or name a new one that does not collide, so the rewrite sent as-is succeeds.
criteria: When the refused join's left key was already cast to the right key's type by an earlier derive of the same name and expression that is still in scope, the rewrite joins on that column and adds no derive; following the advice twice for one text key joined to two integer-keyed datasets ends in a successful transform with the expected rows.
When a column with the cast's name is in scope but was not produced by that same cast, the rewrite derives the cast under a name not in scope, and sent as-is it succeeds.
Tests on data unrelated to any benchmark cover both cases, fail without the fix, and the full suite including the boundary tests passes.
The review thread on PR #3 is answered with what changed.

note: The join key-type refusal now carries the names in scope at the refused step. When an earlier normalized derive has the cast's name and the same cast expression and that column is in scope, the rewrite joins on it and adds no derive, and the explanation says the column was derived earlier; when a column of that name exists otherwise, the cast takes the first free name with a numeric suffix. Following the advice twice for refunds.order_id (text) joined to orders and deliveries (integer keys) now ends in a successful transform with the expected rows, both in a new test and in a replay of the reviewer's scenario. A second new test covers a differently derived column already named order_id_as_integer, where the cast becomes order_id_as_integer_2 and the rewrite succeeds. Both tests fail with the fix stashed; 371 tests pass including the boundary tests. The review thread was answered with the commit, the two cases and the tests, and the PR description was updated.
